article_title: New AI-Driven Tools for Enhancing Campus Well-being: A Prevention and Intervention Approach
citation: Jinwen Tang. (2026). NEW AI-DRIVEN TOOLS FOR ENHANCING CAMPUS WELL-BEING: A PREVENTION AND INTERVENTION APPROACH. Doctoral dissertation, University of Missouri-Columbia. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10804
title: LSDE: a four-dimensional response-quality signal (Length, Self-disclosure, Emotion, Specificity) for adaptive conversational survey control
description: LSDE is the dissertation's multidimensional operationalization of open-ended response quality, capturing "Length, Self-disclosure, Emotion, and Specificity" per exchange. Grounded in survey methodology holding that quality is "multidimensional rather than captured by a single indicator", it yields per-exchange signals suitable for online control in short sessions. AURA uses LSDE as the reward signal that guides within-session selection of follow-up question types.
requirements: Lightweight heuristics or model-based scoring to produce per-exchange quality signals during short 10-15 exchange conversations
constraints: Designed for short sessions of about 10-15 exchanges, which limits the horizon and constrains exploration
target_learners: campus survey respondents (students, faculty, staff, alumni)
target_learning_goals: eliciting deeper, higher-quality open-ended feedback about campus satisfaction and well-being
examples: AURA scores each user response along the four LSDE dimensions and updates expected gains for follow-up question classes such as validate, specify, reflect, and probe
key_sources: Jinwen Tang. (2026). NEW AI-DRIVEN TOOLS FOR ENHANCING CAMPUS WELL-BEING: A PREVENTION AND INTERVENTION APPROACH. Doctoral dissertation, University of Missouri-Columbia. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10804

article_title: Engaging Latinx or Hispanic-Identifying families in science education: A longitudinal intervention study.
citation: Jiang Su, Woodcock Anna, Haddad Kamel, Hernandez Paul R. (2026). Engaging Latinx or Hispanic-Identifying Families in Science Education: A Longitudinal Intervention Study. Journal of Educational Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0001047
title: Latent Trait-State Theory (Revised) applied as a latent single-trait multiple-states model for intervention outcomes
description: LST-R is a longitudinal latent measurement framework distinguishing stable traits from situationally fluctuating states: "latent traits typically change little over time and situations (although trait change is possible), while latent states reflect the influence of persons in situations or person × situation interactions". The article applies its latent single-trait multiple-states model to parent-child outcomes with up to four repeated measures, estimating the ICC for each outcome and testing treatment effects on state variability at T2 and T3 after removing trait variance. It was adopted because prior pre-post designs conflated trait-like and state-like variability.
requirements: At least three repeated measures, per the article's stated assumption that sufficient numbers of repeated measures are assessed
Longitudinal measurement invariance, which the article verified via configural, metric, and scalar invariance testing before estimating treatment effects
constraints: The article acknowledges this latent trait-state modeling approach deviated from the pre-registered ANCOVA analysis plan
Treatment effects estimated under the model apply to state-like person-in-situation variability, not to stable trait-like differences
target_learners: First-year Latinx or Hispanic-identifying STEM undergraduates
examples: The study estimated the model separately for Parent Support, STEM Conversations, STEM Value, and Family Obligations using FIML with auxiliary variables
key_sources: Jiang Su, Woodcock Anna, Haddad Kamel, Hernandez Paul R. (2026). Engaging Latinx or Hispanic-Identifying Families in Science Education: A Longitudinal Intervention Study. Journal of Educational Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0001047

article_title: Beyond boundaries: leveraging technology for differentiated professional development with lesson study video club
citation: Yuzhu Xia, Adria Patthoff, Liana Balloffet, Marco A. Bravo, Kip Téllez. (2025). Beyond boundaries: leveraging technology for differentiated professional development with lesson study video club. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-025-10524-8
title: LSVC hybrid professional development model
description: LSVC is a year-long hybrid teacher PD model that integrates Lesson Study and Video Club principles, using technology (live videoconferencing, teacher-recorded videos, facilitator-selected video content, online asynchronous collaboration tools) to connect teachers across geographies and experience levels. Activities include "whole group workshops, individual self-study, semi-structured conversations with partners, and small group reflective seminars." It was implemented with 71 dual language elementary teachers over three cohorts, and the fully remote format was retained after its benefits became evident.
requirements: Sustained, year-long delivery with cycles of collaborative reflection, full-group discussion, and instructional coaching
Widely available technology for synchronous and asynchronous collaboration
constraints: Delivery varied across the studied years to accommodate COVID-19 pandemic requirements
The model was mediated by shifting district distance-learning requirements during the study period
target_learners: in-service elementary dual language teachers across the career span, from first-year to 27 years of experience
target_learning_goals: integrating language, literacy, and mathematics instruction in dual language settings
bilingual instructional practices and mentoring capability
examples: Three year-long cohorts of 71 DLP teachers in 31 schools across 11 districts in California and Texas participated; 57 completed both pre- and post-surveys.
key_sources: Yuzhu Xia, Adria Patthoff, Liana Balloffet, Marco A. Bravo, Kip Téllez. (2025). Beyond boundaries: leveraging technology for differentiated professional development with lesson study video club. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-025-10524-8

article_title: The Effect of Jumping Task Based on Creative Problem Solving on Students' Problem Solving Ability
citation: Hobri, Ummah, I. K., Yuliati, N., & Dafik (2020). The Effect of Jumping Task Based on Creative Problem Solving on Students’ Problem Solving Ability. International Journal of Instruction, 13(1), 387-406. https://doi.org/10.29333/iji.2020.13126a
title: Lesson Study for Learning Community (LSLC) with four elements including jumping task
description: LSLC is a lesson-study-based framework focusing on how students learn from each other and gain experience working in groups. The article names four elements: jumping task, collaborative learning, caring community, and learning community, stating that jumping task is an element of Lesson Study for Learning Community (LSLC), the other elements of LSLC are collaborative learning, caring community, and learning community. The framework is used to structure the experimental intervention and to explain how difficult tasks plus group interaction build problem-solving ability.
requirements: Group work in which students with high and low ability interact and help each other
Teachers acting as facilitators who provide equal opportunities to convey ideas
constraints: The article reports LSLC's effect on problem solving only when combined with CPS and jumping or sharing tasks in eighth-grade mathematics in Jember, Indonesia
target_learners: eighth-grade junior high school mathematics students
target_learning_goals: collaboration and mutual help in groups
examples: The experimental class x1 was taught with jumping tasks based on CPS within the LSLC elements, with student worksheets consisting of jumping task exercises
key_sources: Hobri, Ummah, I. K., Yuliati, N., & Dafik (2020). The Effect of Jumping Task Based on Creative Problem Solving on Students’ Problem Solving Ability. International Journal of Instruction, 13(1), 387-406. https://doi.org/10.29333/iji.2020.13126a

article_title: A multivariate analysis of the relationships among the Big Five personality traits, activity-oriented learning styles, and academic performance of Grade 12 students in Thailand.
citation: Kaoropthai Chayaporn, Dryver Arthur. (2025). A multivariate analysis of the relationships among the Big Five personality traits, activity-oriented learning styles, and academic performance of Grade 12 students in Thailand. BMC Psychology, 13, 1074. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-025-03387-4
title: The Learning Style Indicator (LSI): a three-factor activity-oriented learning style model for L2 learners
description: The Learning Style Indicator is an alternative learning style model derived from Reid's PLSPQ after exploratory factor analysis showed that PLSPQ items "did not necessarily group into factors conceptually compatible with Reid's learning style model". Its three factors are Group Activity Orientation (GAO), Individual Activity Orientation (IAO), and Project Orientation (PO), clustering items about group interaction, individual learning activities, and class projects. The study used Thai-translated LSI scales to classify Grade 12 EFL students and reports the scales were proved practical and appropriate for this population.
requirements: Respondents complete the LSI scales, translated and validated for the target language context (the study used double back-translation into Thai)
constraints: The article notes the IPIP and LSI instruments may carry cultural biases in translation and recommends validation in Thai contexts
target_learning_goals: Identifying students' preferred activity-oriented learning styles to inform instruction in English and other subjects
examples: The study administered the LSI (GAO 5 items, IAO 7 items, PO 11 items) to 1,088 Grade 12 Thai students and classified their dominant learning style
key_sources: Kaoropthai Chayaporn, Dryver Arthur. (2025). A multivariate analysis of the relationships among the Big Five personality traits, activity-oriented learning styles, and academic performance of Grade 12 students in Thailand. BMC Psychology, 13, 1074. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-025-03387-4

article_title: Application of peer-assisted learning under the LSPPDM mode in resident clinical skill training.
citation: Jin Peipei, Chen Jinyu, Wang Ping, Xie Yadian, Zhang Cen, Shen Liqiong, He Li, Ye Yanqing. (2025). Application of peer-assisted learning under the LSPPDM mode in resident clinical skill training. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-06813-8
title: LSPPDM (Learn, See, Practice, Prove, Do, Maintain) framework for clinical skill training
description: The LSPPDM model is "a framework for teaching clinical skills" that sequences six phases: Learn (online courses, videos and rating tables studied in advance), See (teacher demonstration and observation), Practice (small-group role-rotated practice with peer checklist feedback), Prove (video assessment scored by teachers and peers), Do (operating on real patients during clinical rotation), and Maintain (maintaining skill level through constant practice and staged examinations). The article integrates peer mutual learning into each phase.
requirements: Requires an SRT information management platform for sharing videos and rating tables, a skills center with reservable training rooms, and at least two people training together to strengthen peer learning
constraints: In this study the mode was limited to basic clinical skills course training and has not been applied to more teaching scenarios
target_learners: medical residents in standardized residency training
target_learning_goals: basic clinical skills including internal medicine, surgery and first-aid procedures
examples: Groups of 3 residents rotated master operator and two assistant roles, with assistants rating the main operator against a checklist
key_sources: Jin Peipei, Chen Jinyu, Wang Ping, Xie Yadian, Zhang Cen, Shen Liqiong, He Li, Ye Yanqing. (2025). Application of peer-assisted learning under the LSPPDM mode in resident clinical skill training. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-06813-8

article_title: Impact of laparoscopic training course for surgical trainees based on an evidence-based pedagogical framework: randomized trial.
citation: Pan Ruijun, Zhou Xueliang, Wu Chao, Zhang Luyang, Wang Jiayu, Zheng Minhua, Shi Ting, Cai Wei, Sun Jing. (2024). Impact of laparoscopic training course for surgical trainees based on an evidence-based pedagogical framework: randomized trial. BJS Open. https://doi.org/10.1093/bjsopen/zrae109
title: LSPPDM six-step pedagogical framework for procedural skills training
description: The 'Learn, See, Practice, Prove, Do, Maintain' framework is an evidence-based pedagogical framework developed through review and synthesis of the literature for teaching procedural skills. The article describes it as "a step-by-step process consisting of six steps", divided into a cognitive stage (learn, see) and a psychomotor phase (practice, prove, do, maintain), progressing from lectures, demonstrations and video through simulator practice and summative assessment to supervised clinical practice and lifelong maintenance. In this trial it structured a laparoscopic training course for surgical residents.
requirements: Trainees progress sequentially from 'virtual simulation' to 'live animal' and ultimately to 'clinical practice', with simulator-based assessment passed before operating on patients under supervision
constraints: The 'maintain' step is carried out throughout the trainee's career, so full-framework effects extend beyond a single course
examples: The pedagogical group received 2 lectures/week + video + 2 skills sessions/week, a 30-min instructional video shared by email, simulator practice with an Operational Assessment Sheet, weekly operating theatre rotations, and an extra hour per week of self-directed learning
key_sources: Pan Ruijun, Zhou Xueliang, Wu Chao, Zhang Luyang, Wang Jiayu, Zheng Minhua, Shi Ting, Cai Wei, Sun Jing. (2024). Impact of laparoscopic training course for surgical trainees based on an evidence-based pedagogical framework: randomized trial. BJS Open. https://doi.org/10.1093/bjsopen/zrae109

article_title: IMPACT OF A SIMULATED LAPAROSCOPIC TRAINING PROGRAM IN A THREE-YEAR GENERAL SURGERY RESIDENCY.
citation: Tejos R, Avila R, Inzunza M, Achurra P, Castillo R, Rosberg A, Cordero O, Kusanovich R, Bellolio F, Varas J, Martínez J. (2019). IMPACT OF A SIMULATED LAPAROSCOPIC TRAINING PROGRAM IN A THREE-YEAR GENERAL SURGERY RESIDENCY. Arquivos Brasileiros de Cirurgia Digestiva. https://doi.org/10.1590/0102-672020190001e1436
title: Laparoscopic simulated training program (LSTP): competency-based basic and advanced simulation courses mandatory in PGY1
description: The LSTP is a validated simulation curriculum incorporated into the PUC general surgery residency since 2010, consisting of "two validated courses for acquiring basic and advanced laparoscopic dexterity". The basic course combines FLS and virtual reality exercises over 25 to 50 hours with 12 sequential complexity stations; the advanced course lasts 40 to 50 hours using ex-vivo tissue and requires performing a laparoscopic jejuno-jejunostomy in under 20 minutes. Completion in PGY1 is mandatory to progress to PGY2, and effective feedback with deliberate practice is a central component.
requirements: Residents must complete the courses in PGY1; otherwise, they cannot continue to PGY2
constraints: The advanced LSTP requires a laparoscopic jejuno-jejunostomy in less than 20 minutes as a final complex-task assessment
target_learning_goals: basic and advanced laparoscopic psychomotor skills
examples: Since 2010 the PUC GSR program incorporated the LSTP, becoming the first Latin-American university to include this educational method in its formal curriculum
key_sources: Tejos R, Avila R, Inzunza M, Achurra P, Castillo R, Rosberg A, Cordero O, Kusanovich R, Bellolio F, Varas J, Martínez J. (2019). IMPACT OF A SIMULATED LAPAROSCOPIC TRAINING PROGRAM IN A THREE-YEAR GENERAL SURGERY RESIDENCY. Arquivos Brasileiros de Cirurgia Digestiva. https://doi.org/10.1590/0102-672020190001e1436
